analysis.title: Macro Volatility Digest: Retail Turns Bearish on NVDA Ahead of Earnings (November 16, 2026)
key_insights: Implied vols were mixed across assets last week as risk sentiment improved. The VIX fell over 6 pts to 19.3% (83rd percentile), erasing the prior week's gains, and the VIXIG credit vol index fell almost 8 pts to the 54th percentile.
Bond yields rose despite lower oil prices after the Fed signaled a more hawkish stance. The US 10Y real yield rose 27 bps to about 2.9%.
A hike at the December FOMC is fully priced. The OIS market also prices a roughly 7% probability of a 50 bp hike.
Gold fell to a 1-year low on higher real yields. GLD 1M implied vol rose 0.3 pt to 24%, and GLD 1M 25-delta skew rose to the 83rd percentile on increased put demand.
QQQ led the decline in equity vol as tech rebounded. QQQ 1M implied vol fell 7.3 pts versus 4.5 pts for SPX. SPX 1M implied vol is the richest of the major index vols, in the 77th percentile.
The QQQ-SPX 1M implied vol spread narrowed from a high of 11.7% to 6.8%. The RTY-SPX spread widened from 1.9% to 4.4%, with small caps seen as more vulnerable to higher rates.
SPX and QQQ skew flattened last week, while RTY 1M skew (25-delta ratio) steepened to near a 1-year high.
NVDA reports earnings Tuesday following the ouster of Jensen Huang. Options imply an 8% one-day move, against an average realized earnings move of 4.8% over the past four quarters.
NVDA 1M implied vol rose 2 pts to near a 1-year high of 59%, against 55% realized. Skew flattened on the stock's sell-off, which the report reads as overall bullish sentiment.

Retail positioning in NVDA turned more cautious. Put buying was 32% of retail opening trades on Thursday, over 10 pts above the YTD average of 21%. Call buying is still the bulk of retail activity but has slipped to near the YTD average of about 46%, from a high of 62% in September.
earnings_insights: NVDA reports earnings Tuesday (Nov 17). Options imply a one-day move of 8%, versus an average realized move of 4.8% over the past four quarters. This is an options-implied figure, not a consensus estimate.
